newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes firm on wheat, soybean gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes firm on wheat, soybean gains.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firm on rallies in wheat and soybean futures, traders said.
Trading was quiet and volume was trimmed with position squaring noted before the release Thursday of USDA's world and U.S. supply/demand reports and weekly export sales report.
"Just short covering ahead of the sales tomorrow and s and d report," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co of supportive influences.
The market was underpinned by commercial buying but that demand soon waned which allowed prices to drift.
Traders said a sharp drop in the Dow Jones Industrial average may have weighed on the market.

Cargill Inc bought one million bushels of March and one half million each of May and December, traders said. Term Commodities bought one million bushels of March and Iowa Grain sold one million bushels of March, traders said.

Analysts expect very little change in Thursday's USDA supply/demand balance sheet for corn and traders expected U.S. net export sales of corn for the week ended December 5 to total from 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Corn closed 3/4 to two cents per bushel higher, with December up one at $2.67-1/2 a bushel.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, below the 53,311 contracts traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 700 March $2.70 calls at five to 5-1/4 cents and LIT America sold 400 March $2.90 calls at 1-1/8 to 1-3/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, slightly below the 12,261 traded Tuesday.
